rows.fastIdentity: D_slow^alpha D_v^(b+1)w=D_slow^alpha D_v^b(Mw); every right-hand solution derivative has smaller total order.

volterra.estimate: Every slow/fast derivative word of total length m satisfies ||D^m w||_infinity <= W^(m+1)*(B*S)^powers[m].
premises: S>=1, B>=max(2,Lmax), W>=1, L<=Lmax*S.
The SAME original homogeneous initial datum is independent of all slow coordinates.
The original propagator obeys ||V(v,s)||<=W for 0<=s<=v<=L.
Every actual mixed coefficient derivative of order j has induced infinity norm <=(B*S)^matrixPowers[j].
volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. No order-dependent growth exp(L) is introduced.

mixed.base: B_m>=max(Bnorm,C_(m+2),(m+2)!,Lmax,2^128), fixed independently of ell, labels and representative; S=ell^2>=1.

sourcePremises.background: Every original slow derivative of F,G through m+2 is bounded by C_(m+2) on the same enlarged source annulus, for the same common recursive cutoff sequence.
sourcePremises.normal: n=(x0-v*H_R,p/R,pz-epsilon*v*H_Z), H=p*F+pz*G. Both H_R and H_Z retain all mixed slow derivatives. Frozen p,pz,x0 and their source scales, R^-1 and reference data obey the unchanged Bnorm bounds. epsilon<=1 and 0<=v<=L<=Lmax*S. Leibniz and derivatives of 1/R then give |D^j n_i|<=(B_m*S)^(j+16); the extra power16 retains all finite products and sums.
sourcePremises.positiveFloors: The unchanged source has |n_tan|,|n|>=Bnorm^-2, |c0|>=Bnorm^-1 and sqrt(1+sref^2)>=1. These imply the weaker (B_m*S) floors used by the exact reciprocal/sqrt recurrence.
sourcePremises.frozenReference: P, c0, lambda0, sref, dref and every frozen representative/carrier are slow independent inside each fixed-label chart; v derivatives of the reference data are retained.
sourcePremises.stable: The actual original matrix has mu_infinity(M)<=(2E+Ed)/S; hence its propagator is bounded by fixed W=exp((2E+Ed)*Lmax). Use the original positive Gaussian envelope P(v).

mixed.estimate: For every fixed total slow/fast order m, ||D^m t||_infinity <= W^(m+1)*(B_m*S)^powers.t[m]*P(v). At positive temporal-cutoff derivatives, P(v)<=exp(-a*ell^2) with the SAME a>0.

inputNormalization.neighboringInputConstant: A local-label source bound F_m*S_label^b first contributes 4^b to the common-reference input F_m; every epsilon/zeta/chart ratio must also be retained there.

backgroundPrefix.proof: Only coefficient/frame/P prefixes through m are consumed. Their n-prime entries use n through m+1 and hence F,G through m+2. The extra generic ledger rows beyond that prefix are not asserted under this lower background bound.

forced.coefficientConstantBase: K_m>=max(2, B_m, maximum absolute harmonic, Lmax, all fixed affine common-torus factors).
forced.estimate: Every derivative through m is bounded by the common-reference input F_m*W^(m+1)*(K_m*S_ref)^p times its retained reference epsilon/zeta/pole factors and P; pressure gains sqrt(epsilon_ref), with any local/reference epsilon ratio included in F_m.

premises: S>=1, B>=max(2,Lmax), W>=1, L<=Lmax*S.

volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. sourcePremises.background: Every original slow derivative of F,G through m+2 is bounded by C_(m+2) on the same enlarged source annulus, for the same common recursive cutoff sequence.

volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. premises: S>=1, B>=max(2,Lmax), W>=1, L<=Lmax*S.

volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. premises: S>=1, B>=max(2,Lmax), W>=1, L<=Lmax*S.

volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. No order-dependent growth exp(L) is introduced.
